brief.headline: Force Claude Code to prove its work before it says 'done'
brief.summary:
Two separate repos landed on the same fix this cycle: fablize turns Opus in Claude Code into a plugin that must produce evidence and pass verification before it reports a task finished, and fable-method ships the underlying think/act/prove skills plus eval if you'd rather build your own gate. Pair either with loop-engineering's loop-audit and loop-cost CLIs and you've got most of a verify-then-report loop for overnight runs. Claude Code 2.1.221 also adds a sandbox "mask" mode so unattended agents can read credential-bearing files on Linux/WSL without exposing real secrets — worth flipping on before your next long run.

On spend, a cluster of proxies (opencodex, claudexor, omnigent, scasella's Codex backend) now sit in front of Claude Code and Codex so you can swap in cheaper or local models — DeepSeek, Gemini, Ollama — without rewriting your existing scripts, or rotate across subscriptions when one hits its quota mid-run. DeepSeek-V4's dao-code and AirLLM's 70B-on-4GB-GPU trick push the cheap-inference floor even lower for routine subagent work. Hoplite is a fresh option for running your local Claude Code setup — sessions, MCP servers included — in a cloud sandbox, and Boris Cherny's own account of trying to get Claude Code to rewrite the Claude app is a useful reality check on where big unattended rewrites still need a human checkpoint.
bullets: Install the fivetaku/fablize Claude Code plugin to make Opus produce evidence and pass verification before it marks a task complete
Clone Sahir619/fable-method for the portable think/act/prove skills and eval if you want to build the gate yourself
Point Claude Code or Codex at lidge-jun/opencodex or razzant/claudexor to route subagent calls to cheaper backends or rotate across subscriptions when one hits quota
Try tigicion/dao-code for DeepSeek-V4 with byte-stable cache prefixes, keeping your existing Skills/MCP/Hooks config
Set sandbox mode "mask" in Claude Code 2.1.221 so unattended agents can safely touch credential files on Linux/WSL
Watch overnight spend across every tool with Javis603/token-monitor's local desktop widget

items.title: cobusgreyling/loop-engineering — Practical patterns, starters & CLI tools for loop engineering with AI coding agents. Design systems that prompt and orchestrate agents (inspired by Addy Osmani and Boris Cherny). Includes loop-audit, loop-in
items.tldr: The loop-engineering repo ships CLI tools — loop-init, loop-audit, loop-cost — for designing and orchestrating AI coding-agent loops.
items.whyItMatters: loop-audit and loop-cost directly target self-verification and spend-tracking for agent runs, the two things the reader is trying to build into his own unattended workflow.
items.tryThis: Clone cobusgreyling/loop-engineering and run loop-init to scaffold a verify-then-report loop, then use loop-cost to track spend per agent run.

items.tldr: Claude Code 2.1.221 adds a VSCode Focus view (Ctrl+Alt+F) that collapses tool activity into a per-turn summary, plus a sandbox 'mask' mode that lets sandboxed commands read masked credential files while real values are substituted on egress.
items.whyItMatters: The credential-mask mode is a direct way to let unattended agents touch secret-bearing files/commands more safely on Linux/WSL.
items.tryThis: Set sandbox mode: "mask" for credential files in your Claude Code config on Linux/WSL and try Focus view with Ctrl+Alt+F in VSCode.

items.title: Quoting David Crawshaw's prompt
items.tldr: David Crawshaw's nightly cron prompt tells an agent to fetch upstream changes, rebase local changes on top, verify the software still works, and swap in the new version.
items.whyItMatters: It's a ready-made unattended-maintenance loop — exactly the 'describe the work, wake up to a result' pattern the reader is chasing for keeping his own tools/dependencies current.
items.tryThis: Add a nightly cron job running: 'fetch upstream changes, rebase local changes on top, verify it works, then replace the current version' against one of your own forked/vendored dependencies.

items.title: omnigent-ai/omnigent — Omnigent is an open-source AI agent framework and meta-harness: orchestrate Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, and custom agents — swap harnesses without rewriting, enforce policies and sandboxing, and collaborate in rea
items.tldr: omnigent is an open-source meta-harness that orchestrates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Pi agents interchangeably with policy enforcement, sandboxing, and control from any device.
items.whyItMatters: Gives him a single control plane to swap harnesses per task and manage running agents remotely instead of being locked into one CLI session.
items.tryThis: Clone omnigent-ai/omnigent and wire it in front of your Claude Code worktrees to test cross-device control and policy enforcement.

items.title: lidge-jun/opencodex — Universal provider proxy for OpenAI Codex & Claude Code — use any LLM (Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama…) with Codex CLI, App, SDK, and Claude Code
items.tldr: opencodex is a proxy that lets Codex CLI and Claude Code call any backend LLM — Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Ollama.
items.whyItMatters: Lets him route cheap or local models into his existing Claude Code/Codex agent scripts without rewriting them.
items.tryThis: Clone lidge-jun/opencodex and point Codex CLI/Claude Code's provider config at it to test a cheaper backend for routine subagent tasks.

items.title: nexu-io/html-video — Programmatic video for coding agents — HTML to video on your laptop. Turn HTML, CSS & data into real MP4s with pluggable render engines, 21 templates, AI soundtrack. Apache-2.0, no per-render fees. An official project b
items.tldr: nexu-io/html-video renders HTML, CSS, and data into real MP4s locally via pluggable engines, Apache-2.0 licensed with no per-render fees.
items.whyItMatters: Gives agents a cheap, local way to attach visual proof-of-work (demo videos of UI changes) to a PR for morning review.
items.tryThis: Clone nexu-io/html-video and wire it into your CI/PR pipeline to auto-render a demo MP4 of UI diffs overnight.

items.title: Sahir619/fable-method — The Fable Workflow: how Claude Fable 5 worked, distilled into skills any model can run, with the eval that keeps it honest. Think / act / prove.
items.tldr: A new repo distills the 'Fable' workflow into portable skills plus an eval that enforces think/act/prove on any model.
items.whyItMatters: Directly targets getting an agent to verify its own work before calling a task done — the core blocker to unattended overnight runs.
items.tryThis: Clone Sahir619/fable-method and wire its skills + eval harness into your Claude Code project so a run must produce evidence before it's marked complete.

items.title: tigicion/dao-code — Open-source TypeScript terminal coding agent for DeepSeek-V4 — builds on DeepSeek's strong price-performance and ultra-cheap cache pricing, engineering byte-stable prefixes and cache-reusing forks so cross-session memory
items.tldr: dao-code is an open-source terminal coding agent for DeepSeek-V4 that engineers byte-stable prompt prefixes so cache reuse keeps cross-session memory almost free.
items.whyItMatters: A DeepSeek-based, Claude Code-config-compatible agent gives him a much cheaper unattended option with 1M context and existing Skills/MCP/Hooks support.
items.tryThis: Clone tigicion/dao-code and reuse your Claude Code Skills/MCP/Hooks config to test DeepSeek-V4 pricing on a subagent.

items.title: Javis603/token-monitor — Local-first desktop widget for tracking token usage, costs, and limits across 28+ AI coding tools—including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and OpenClaw—with multi-device sync.
items.tldr: token-monitor is a local-first desktop widget tracking token usage, cost, and limits across 28+ AI coding tools with multi-device sync.
items.whyItMatters: One dashboard to watch overnight agent spend across every tool he mixes instead of checking each vendor's console.
items.tryThis: Install Javis603/token-monitor and enable multi-device sync to watch overnight agent-run cost in real time.

items.title: fivetaku/fablize — A Claude Code plugin that makes Opus behave like Fable — completion, evidence, and verification enforced as procedure. Ships only what a Fable-vs-Opus comparison proved transferable.
items.tldr: A Claude Code plugin, fablize, makes Opus enforce the same completion/evidence/verification procedure that Fable used.
items.whyItMatters: Drop-in plugin form of self-verification for Claude Code specifically — closer to a reviewable-PR default than a from-scratch prompt.
items.tryThis: Install the fivetaku/fablize Claude Code plugin to force Opus to produce evidence and pass verification before it reports a task finished.

items.title: CodeBendKit/codeseek — Rust-powered code intelligence CLI for AI coding agents. Builds call graphs and hybrid semantic search indexes (Dense + Sparse + RRF + Reranker) across 7 languages. Ships as native MCP tools for Claude Code and Codex
items.tldr: codeseek is a Rust CLI that builds call graphs and hybrid semantic search indexes across 7 languages, exposed as native MCP tools for Claude Code and Codex CLI.
items.whyItMatters: Better code-navigation context means fewer clarifying questions and more accurate unattended edits before a PR lands.
items.tryThis: Install CodeBendKit/codeseek as an MCP server and point your Claude Code config at it for call-graph-aware searches during agent runs.

items.title: razzant/claudexor — Multi-harness control plane for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode: quota-aware rotation across multiple Claude/Codex subscriptions, shared thread context, and cross-model review.
items.tldr: claudexor is a control plane that rotates work across multiple Claude/Codex subscriptions by quota, sharing thread context and enabling cross-model review.
items.whyItMatters: Addresses running agents unattended for long stretches without one account's rate limit stalling the job.
items.tryThis: Clone razzant/claudexor and register your Claude/Codex subscriptions to test quota-aware rotation on a long overnight run.

items.title: scasella/claude-dynamic-workflows-codex — Run Claude Code dynamic workflows on a local Codex (GPT) backend, plus an interactive run viewer
items.tldr: This repo runs Claude Code's dynamic workflow feature against a local Codex (GPT) backend, with an interactive run viewer.
items.whyItMatters: Lets him keep the Workflow/pipeline orchestration he already uses while swapping in a cheaper or local backend for execution.
items.tryThis: Clone scasella/claude-dynamic-workflows-codex and repoint one existing workflow script at the local Codex backend to compare cost and output.

items.title: AirLLM 70B inference with single 4GB GPU
items.tldr: AirLLM shows 70B-parameter model inference running on a single 4GB GPU.
items.whyItMatters: Puts a 70B-class model within reach of consumer hardware he may already own, as a free local backend for low-stakes subagent work.
items.tryThis: Try the AirLLM repo on a spare 4GB+ GPU box to benchmark it as a free local backend for routine subagent tasks.

items.title: DietrichGebert/ponytail — Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
items.tldr: ponytail is a viral repo (95k+ stars) of prompt rules that push an AI coding agent to favor deleting/avoiding code over writing it.
items.whyItMatters: A cheap, drop-in instruction set to fight agent over-engineering and bloat in generated PRs — pairs with your existing simplify-review habit.
items.tryThis: Pull the rules from DietrichGebert/ponytail into a CLAUDE.md instruction so the agent defaults to the smallest diff instead of the most code.

items.title: oomol-lab/open-connector — Open-source auth gateway connecting 1000+ SaaS providers to AI agents through SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP, and OpenAPI.
items.tldr: open-connector is an open-source auth gateway wiring 1000+ SaaS providers to agents via SDK, CLI, MCP, HTTP, and OpenAPI.
items.whyItMatters: Cuts the OAuth-per-integration busywork of hooking your agents up to real services, which matters once agents need to touch more than your git repo.
items.tryThis: Stand up oomol-lab/open-connector as an MCP auth gateway instead of hand-rolling OAuth for each SaaS your agents need to reach.

items.title: Waishnav/devspace — Turn ChatGPT into Codex! OR Turn Claude Web into Claude Code!
items.tldr: devspace drives ChatGPT's web UI like Codex, or Claude's web chat like Claude Code, from the CLI.
items.whyItMatters: Could let him tap an existing ChatGPT Plus/Claude Pro web subscription for agentic coding instead of metered API billing.
items.tryThis: Clone Waishnav/devspace and test it against your web subscription to see if it beats API billing for routine tasks.

items.title: DenisSergeevitch/agents-best-practices — Provider-neutral Agent Skill for Codex, Claude Code, and agentic harness design.
items.tldr: DenisSergeevitch published a provider-neutral Agent Skill covering harness design patterns for Codex and Claude Code.
items.whyItMatters: A drop-in Skill to sanity-check or tighten his own subagent/hook design instead of reinventing prompt structure.
items.tryThis: Install the agents-best-practices Skill into your Claude Code project and diff its patterns against your current hooks/skills setup.

items.title: gi-dellav/zerostack — Lightweight coding agent written in Rust, optimized for memory footprint and performance
items.tldr: gi-dellav/zerostack is a lightweight coding agent written in Rust, optimized for memory footprint and performance.
items.whyItMatters: A leaner self-hosted agent binary is a candidate for cheap, low-resource background or verification passes instead of a full Claude Code session.
items.tryThis: Clone gi-dellav/zerostack and trial it as a low-cost subagent for mechanical verification tasks.

items.title: Boris Cherny on Trying to Get Claude Code to Rewrite the Claude App
items.tldr: Claude Code creator Boris Cherny recounts trying to get Claude Code to rewrite the Claude app itself.
items.whyItMatters: A first-person account from the tool's own lead on where a large agentic rewrite holds up and where it needs a human hand — worth mirroring as checkpoints in your own overnight runs.
items.tryThis: Read the thread for where Cherny had to intervene manually, and set equivalent checkpoints in your own long unattended runs.

items.title: Launch HN: Hoplite (YC S26) – Effortlessly deploy cloud coding agents
items.tldr: YC-backed Hoplite launches a service that ports your local coding-agent setup — sessions, memories, MCP servers — into a cloud sandbox for one-click deployment.
items.whyItMatters: Fits 'describe the work, go to sleep' directly: it's built to run cloud coding-agent sessions with your existing local config, not a from-scratch remote setup.
items.tryThis: Try hoplite.sh to port your Claude Code sessions and MCP servers into a cloud sandbox for overnight or remote-triggered runs.

clusters.title: Verify-before-done plugins from the Fable workflow
clusters.summary: Two repos distill the same 'Fable' think/act/prove procedure — one as a ready Claude Code plugin that makes Opus produce evidence and pass verification before finishing, the other as the underlying portable skills and eval.

clusters.title: Backend-swap control planes for Claude Code/Codex
clusters.summary: A wave of proxies and meta-harnesses let you keep existing Claude Code/Codex workflows while swapping in cheaper or local models, rotating across subscriptions to dodge rate limits, or running on a local Codex backend.

clusters.title: Cheap inference floor gets lower
clusters.summary: Consumer hardware running 70B-class models and cache-priced DeepSeek-V4 agents make offloading routine subagent tasks to cheap or local backends more viable.
